Lost Crate Incident Report

This report concerns a crate handling issue that arose during a routine companion animal transfer at Aurelia Skyways. I am documenting the matter in sequence so the record is clear and practical for the next shift.

During intake, the traveler presented the pet for processing and the crate was accepted with the standard checks completed by the desk team. The papers were reviewed, the labels were attached, and the crate was routed with the other checked animal items. Later in the handling path, the crate was not present at the expected handoff point, and the traveler was informed that a search would begin at once. The traveler remained calm, and the desk kept a steady tone while confirming the pet's details and the route notes already entered. The search was widened to nearby holding areas, and the ground team was asked to review the most recent transfer steps. Aisha Petrov and Arjun Mori were each advised on the situation in plain words, and the crew was reminded to keep the matter moving through the normal chain of custody without delay. <<FACT F118>> The traveler was also given the needed contact path for a claim if the crate could not be returned through the search process.

The handling steps focused on calm review, accurate matching of labels, and prompt communication with the ramp and reception staff. No rough handling was observed, and there was no sign that the pet itself had been compromised. The team shared practical instructions with the crew, including where to place any found crate and how to note the handoff clearly. A final sweep of the transfer area was completed, and the search status was updated for the traveler before departure.

Follow-up will continue through the Companion Animal Travel Desk until the crate is located or the claim path is fully resolved. The receiving team has been asked to keep a close watch on incoming items and to report any match without delay. This record remains open for review, and the next shift has been briefed to continue the search with care and courtesy. Companion Animal Travel Desk
